input.content:
You are building a frozen evidence-source packet for a focused PFAS treatment
review. Use Web Search to locate independent primary studies, pilot or field
deployments, or quantitative modeling/life-cycle studies that directly address
the task. The defining review is held out and is an exclusion target, not an
evidence source.

Search broadly and return every independently verified eligible primary source
found within the requested candidate-screening ceiling. There is no fixed final
source count and no penalty for retaining multiple eligible studies that address
similar evidence categories. Continue searching across distinct formulations
until the ceiling is reached or additional searches yield no new eligible
sources. Order retained sources from strongest and most complementary to
weakest. Favor sources that collectively cover all task components and preserve PFAS identity,
water matrix, concentration or loading, operating conditions, scale, endpoint,
quantitative result, limitations, residuals, energy, and cost where available.
Review articles and perspectives may help discovery but must not appear in the
  source packet.

For every retained source:

- provide the exact URL inspected by Web Search, matching the URL surfaced by
  the search tool rather than substituting a different repository or index;
- provide a DOI when one is stated by the inspected source;
- identify the publication year and publication status conservatively;
- identify the access scope conservatively;
- include only short evidence passages actually visible in the inspected
  source, each with a stable local locator_id;
- mark a passage verbatim only when it is copied exactly; otherwise mark it as
  a paraphrase;
- never turn a search-result snippet into study evidence; and
- leave unsupported fields empty rather than infer them.

Prefer peer-reviewed articles. Use a preprint, conference abstract, or report
only when it supplies distinct task-relevant evidence unavailable from a
peer-reviewed source, and label its status explicitly.

Do not cite, reconstruct, or use the held-out review. Source and locator IDs are
temporary capture identifiers and will be deterministically renumbered after
validation. Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

Focused review task:
{"review_brief":"Prepare a focused review of the measurements needed to distinguish disappearance of a target PFAS from transformation, defluorination, and broader destruction.","task_id":"RT09","title":"Determining whether a PFAS destructive treatment achieved meaningful destruction"}

Required components:
[{"component_id":"RT09-C1","requirement":"Compare parent-compound loss, transformation-product analysis, fluoride release, fluorine mass balance, and mineralization-related endpoints."},{"component_id":"RT09-C2","requirement":"Evaluate how analytical scope, sampling time, detection limits, and unidentified products affect interpretation."},{"component_id":"RT09-C3","requirement":"Define a defensible evidence hierarchy for reporting destruction while preserving technology, matrix, and scale limitations."}]

Task-specific extraction objective:
Extract treatment and conditions, parent PFAS measurement, transformation-product scope, fluoride or fluorine measurement, mass-balance method, mineralization-related endpoint, detection limits, sampling time, unidentified fraction, and authors' endpoint terminology.

search_notes: Search targeted primary experimental and pilot studies quantifying PFAS destruction endpoints: parent-compound loss, transformation products, fluoride release, fluorine mass balance, and mineralization proxies across diverse technologies (UV/sulfite, UV/sulfite/iodide, ultrasound, hydrothermal alkaline treatment, smoldering thermal treatment, and supercritical water oxidation).
Review and perspective articles (e.g., on fluorine mass balance needs) were used only for discovery and deliberately excluded from the evidence packet, as required.

Where publisher sites (ACS, Elsevier, ScienceDirect) returned 403 or reCAPTCHA barriers, alternative open-access repositories (institutional repositories, theses, PMC, enviro.wiki, ChemRxiv, UCL Discovery, ResearchGate) were searched to obtain full texts or author manuscripts.

Several promising recent studies (e.g., high-frequency ultrasound fluorine mass balance paper; some UV/sulfite mechanistic work) could not be inspected beyond abstracts due to access limitations and were therefore not retained as sources, to avoid using search-result snippets as evidence.

Within the 20-source ceiling, saturation for high-quality, directly relevant primary sources appeared after identifying multiple complementary technologies each with quantified defluorination and at least partial fluorine mass balance; additional searches began to return overlapping work, reviews, or sources inaccessible beyond abstract level.

sources.citation: Ren Z, Bergmann U, Leiviskä T. Reductive degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid in complex water matrices by using the UV/sulfite process. Water Research. 2021;205:117676.

evidence_passages.page_or_section: Page 2, Section 2.2 Reductive degradation of PFOA

source_limitations: Single-target study focused on PFOA; does not include other PFAS classes.
Defluorination is tracked via fluoride ISE; total fluorine or organofluorine mass balance is not closed.
Matrix complexity is represented by added inorganic anions and humic acid rather than real field samples.
Detection limit for PFOA (10 μg/L) may not be representative of state-of-the-art analytical sensitivity.
sources.title: Reductive degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid in complex water matrices by using the UV/sulfite process

sources.citation: O’Connor N. Forever No More: Complete mineralization of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) using an optimized UV/sulfite/iodide system. In: Aqueous Electron Initiated Destruction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS). PhD thesis, Royal Military College of Canada; 2024. Chapter 3. Related journal article: Sci Total Environ. 2023;888:164137.
source_limitations: Thesis format; overlapping content with a peer-reviewed article but thesis itself is not peer-reviewed.
Emphasis on relatively high PFAS concentrations compared with typical environmental waters.
Fluoride recovery is emphasized, but full fluorine mass balance including volatile organofluorine is not comprehensively closed.
Matrix complexity is evaluated mainly with bicarbonate buffer and added scavengers rather than real wastewaters.
sources.title: Forever No More: Complete mineralization of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) using an optimized UV/sulfite/iodide system (thesis chapter)

sources.citation: Pinkard B, Smith SM, Vorarath P, et al. Degradation and Defluorination of Ultra Short‑, Short‑, and Long-Chain PFASs in High Total Dissolved Solids Solutions by Hydrothermal Alkaline Treatment—Closing the Fluorine Mass Balance. ACS ES&T Engineering. 2024;4:2810–2818.
source_limitations: Bench-scale study using synthetic high-TDS solutions; not direct field implementation.
Focus is on aqueous phase; volatile organofluorine species are inferred to be minimal but not directly trapped in a gas-phase train.
HALT conditions (250–350 °C, high NaOH) differ substantially from many competing destruction technologies and are specific to concentrated brines.
Study is designed around a specific mixture of PFAS and does not include polymeric PFAS.
sources.title: Degradation and Defluorination of Ultra Short‑, Short‑, and Long-Chain PFASs in High Total Dissolved Solids Solutions by Hydrothermal Alkaline Treatment—Closing the Fluorine Mass Balance

sources.citation: Smith SM, Pinkard BR, Zweifel T, et al. Demonstration of hydrothermal alkaline treatment for PFAS destruction in industrial wastewater: assessment of degradation, defluorination, fluorine mass balance, and potential for volatile organofluorine formation. ChemRxiv; 2025. Preprint.
source_limitations: Preprint; not yet peer-reviewed at time of inspection.
Industrial wastewater composition and PFAS profile are specific to an ion-exchange regeneration brine and may not generalize to other matrices.
Fluorine mass balance does not include direct quantitative speciation of all volatile organofluorine compounds at sub-trace levels.
Focus is on fluorinated carboxylic acids (FCAs); perfluoroalkyl sulfonic acids are present only as minor constituents.
sources.title: Demonstration of hydrothermal alkaline treatment for PFAS destruction in industrial wastewater: assessment of degradation, defluorination, fluorine mass balance, and potential for volatile organofluorine formation

source_limitations: Soil-GAC systems spiked with PFOS-dominant PFAS mixture; may not represent all contaminated soil types.
Total fluorine measurements by PIGE have relatively high detection limits and cannot distinguish organic vs inorganic fluorine.
Fluorine mass balance uncertainties are large, with recoveries ranging from 68% to 128%.
Transformation products are characterized only at ultralow concentrations in emissions; many minor products remain unidentified.

source_limitations: Single-compound study focusing on PFOS; results may not extend to mixed PFAS or AFFF matrices.
Fluorine mass balance is evaluated primarily via inorganic fluoride and targeted short-chain PFAAs; volatile organofluorine species are not comprehensively quantified.
Experiments conducted in relatively simple aqueous solutions, not complex natural waters or waste streams.
Detection limits and quantitation limits for transformation products are not always explicitly tied to mass-balance closure.

source_limitations: Study evaluates parent PFAS removal kinetics but does not quantify fluoride or total defluorination, limiting conclusions about mineralization.
Short-chain PFAS transformation products are monitored, but fluorine mass balance is not closed.

Argon sparging and laboratory reactor geometry may not directly translate to full-scale systems.
